subject: Pricing parity request: seat tiers & migration-credit structuring
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pricing parity vs CloudForge + migration credits

Marcus —

Quick note following our procurement review: Acme has a competing offer from CloudForge that includes a blended seat-based rate for inference and a 3-month migration credit (they quoted an onboarding allowance and 20% discounted seat tiers for the first 6 months). We like Redwood from a runtime and reliability perspective, but procurement is pushing for price parity (seat-tier parity) and an explicit migration-credit structure to cover integration effort.

I attached our RFP and the competitor quote so you can see the numbers (Acme_RFP.pdf; competitor_quote_cloudforge.pdf). Key asks:
- Can Redwood match the effective blended seat price at the 10k-seat tier?
- Would you consider a 3–6 month migration credit (either cash/credit bucket or token credit)?
- Any limited-term SLA or onboarding support you can attach to the commitment to reduce our ops risk?

We’re not asking for indefinite discounting — just a short-term concession to make the TCO comparable and move forward quickly.

Can you send a short commercial sketch by EOD tomorrow? Procurement will need a high-level letter with proposed credits to circulate.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform
Acme Analytics

Attachments: Acme_RFP.pdf (pdf), competitor_quote_cloudforge.pdf (pdf)

Jordan —

Thanks for sending this and for the clear asks. Appreciated. We can absolutely put together a short commercial sketch — a couple clarifying questions to make sure the proposal aligns with Acme’s objectives:
1) When you say "effective blended seat price at the 10k-seat tier," are you referencing the competitor's list price or their committed effective rate after their promotional buckets? The attachment is helpful but I want to match apples-to-apples (runtime minutes / token-equivalent / seat definition).
2) Is the migration credit meant to cover professional services hours (integration + validation) or purely consumption credit? We have both playbooks.
3) What SLA uplift would move the needle for procurement — lower P99 latency SLOs, guaranteed throughput, or an onboarding SLA (time-to-first-50k-requests)?

High-level response: we can do an equivalent seat-rate parity via a limited-term tiered discount and offer a migration-credit bucket (either as 3 months of consumption credit or a $X onboarding credit) plus a dedicated onboarding SRE window. I’ll loop in our sales director to finalize the exact numbers.

I’ll follow up with a draft today.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Can you propose the concession structure we typically use (tiered seat discount + migration credit bucket + onboarding SRE)? If we can keep the economic impact to <10% ARR equivalent in year 1 via a time-limited credit and ramp schedule, I think we can do it.

Also copying Kim for implementation/ops cost estimates.

Thanks —

Thanks for the context — good opportunity. Proposal sketch below (numbers are draft and subject to legal/finance sign-off):

1) Seat-tier parity:
- Offer a time-limited "10k-seat parity" bundle: 12-month committed agreement with effective blended rate matching the CloudForge committed effective price for the first 12 months. After 12 months revert to standard tier pricing.
- If we need to anchor to token-equivalents, we map their seat definition to our token-hour run-rate; Finance will validate effective $/vector-hour parity.

2) Migration credit:
- Provide a 90-day consumption credit equal to 100% of projected consumption for the first 30 days, then 50% for days 31–90 (applied as account credit). Equivalent to a 3-month graduated consumption credit.
- Credit is non-transferable, expires after 90 days, and only applies to production usage (not POC/dev buckets).

3) Onboarding SRE & SLA:
- Dedicated onboarding SRE for the first 30 days (40 hours/week) including two guaranteed ramp-checks and a P99 latency target for that period.
- Add a clause: if regional availability dips below 99.9% during onboarding and the issue is on our side, a further one-time credit of X days will be applied.

4) Contract language and guardrails:
- Include a clawback if the customer significantly overstates baseline usage (standard audit language).
- Set a minimum commitment floor (to protect unit economics) at 70% of the 10k-seat committed run-rate.

Attachments: proposed_terms_v1.docx — contains commercial sketch and draft contract language for legal.

Estimated first-year economic impact: roughly a low-single-digit % of ARR if they hit committed usage; worst-case (if they burn credits and then churn) higher but protected by the minimum-commitment floor.

If Marcus is comfortable with this sketch I’ll convert to a single-page commercial letter for Jordan and pricing worksheet for Finance. Kim — can you confirm operational feasibility and any additional migration-cost estimate?

—Connor Obrien
